sections.h2: Who do I call about a Wayne County, KY tax bill?
sections.html:
Monticello has all three desks. One office values the parcel, one collects the money, and one picks up the leftovers: PVA, Sheriff, and County Clerk, in that order through the year.

The PVA sits at 55 N. Main Street, Suite 107, Monticello, KY 42633, phone 606-348-6621. Beyond the usual weekday hours of 8 to 4, the county advertises Saturday service on the first and third Saturday of the month, 8 a.m. to noon. That is the easiest time for a working owner to ask about a value or an exemption. For a lost bill or a payment question, ask the Sheriff's Office in Monticello for its current phone and window hours.

Rates are not the PVA's business. The fiscal court, school board, and special districts vote them, and the PVA stops at the assessed value.

sections.h2: What does paying late cost in Wayne County?
sections.html:
Each month of delay costs money, on the schedule of KRS 134.015, and the Sheriff takes payment until April 15. Pay everything by November 1 and 2 percent comes off. After January 31 the extra charge tops out at 10 percent.

  • On or before November 1: bill less 2 percent.
  • Rest of November and December: the number printed on the bill.
  • During January: 5 percent more.
  • February 1 to April 15: 10 percent more.

A late mailing from Frankfort allows an alternative calendar of 30-day blocks, so count from the mailing date shown on your own bill, not from the dates here.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Wayne County assessment?
sections.html:
A conversation at the PVA's counter has to come first. State rules do not allow an appeal to be filed without it, and the staff must explain the valuation method and keep notes. Then the steps below apply.

Appeal steps for Wayne County property owners
StepWhen
Public inspection of the roll13 days beginning the first Monday in May
Talk with the PVAAnytime after notices go out, before filing
Written appeal at the County ClerkClose of business the day after inspection ends
Hearing before the local board25 to 35 days after inspection, up to five days of sessions

The board wants proof it can see: insurance policies, construction cost, listings, and the physical features of land and buildings. Owners near Lake Cumberland should document docks, decks, and outbuildings as they stood on January 1. Missing the hearing after filing cuts off a further appeal.

sections.h2: Can a senior in Wayne County pay less property tax?
sections.html:
Yes, through the homestead exemption, which lifts $49,100 off the assessed value of an owner's own residence for 2025 and 2026. Applicants are 65 or older, or classified as totally disabled by a federal agency or a retirement system.

Try it with the Census median value for Wayne County owner-occupied homes, $135,700. The taxable figure falls to $86,600. Using the state's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents per $100, the state's share goes from roughly $143.84 to roughly $91.80. Local districts add their own rates, so ask the PVA for a combined number.

  • Apply at the Wayne County PVA; the form is the state's homestead and disability application.
  • Proof of age can be a passport, license, or birth certificate.
  • Disability payments must have been received through the whole assessment period.
  • Owners with a service-connected veteran disability, or a permanent total ruling from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems, are spared yearly renewal.

sections.h2: Do unpaid Wayne County taxes block a sale?
sections.html:
Not by themselves, but they come out of your proceeds. A lien tied to the delinquent bill remains on the parcel for up to 11 years under KRS 134.420, whoever holds the deed, so buyers' title companies insist on payoff.

The first Clerk-stage bill starts from the face amount, adds a 10 percent penalty and the Sheriff's add-on, then collects 1 percent interest each month. Commissions for the clerk and county attorney, mailing costs, and a lien recording fee follow. In the Revenue Department's model, a $1,000 bill reaches $1,254 on transfer and about $1,611 once the first notice is out.

A sale of the certificate to an outside investor can occur 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and the investor may add its own charges. Settle with the Sheriff before April 15 to avoid that path, and write the current-year split into the sales contract.

sections.h2: What is Wayne County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
On the Tennessee border, Wayne County was cut from Pulaski and Cumberland counties on December 13, 1800, and honors General Anthony Wayne. Monticello is the lone city and the seat. About 458 square miles of land reach into the Daniel Boone National Forest and meet Lake Cumberland, a reservoir the county's website credits with 1,255 miles of shoreline. Mill Springs was the scene of the January 19, 1862 battle that ended with the Confederate commander's death.

Time zones matter here. Wayne County uses Eastern time, but its western and southern edges follow the Eastern and Central boundary, so a lender, buyer, or attorney across the line may be an hour off. Public schools belong to Wayne County Schools, which absorbed Monticello Independent on June 30, 2013, and the Area Technology Center teaches welding, carpentry, health science, and other trades.

  • Population 19,597 in 2025, up 0.2 percent from 2020 but below the 20,813 of 2010.
  • 10,206 housing units against 8,074 households, a 2,132 unit difference.
  • 69.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied, at a median value of $135,700.
  • Median household income is $45,739, and 28.8 percent of residents are in poverty.
  • Median gross rent is $727, and 22.7 percent of residents are 65 or older.

The county is also known for folk music: fiddler Dick Burnett, who wrote "Man of Constant Sorrow," was born near Monticello. Owners with inherited cabins, rentals, or homes that need work can sell as-is for cash and settle taxes at the closing table.

faqs.q: What are the Wayne County PVA's hours?
faqs.a: The PVA, at 55 N. Main Street, Suite 107 in Monticello, is open weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and the first and third Saturday of each month from 8 a.m. to noon. Call 606-348-6621.

faqs.q: How much can I save by paying Wayne County tax early?
faqs.a: Two percent, if the whole bill is paid by November 1. After December 31 penalties of 5 percent, then 10 percent, apply.

faqs.q: Is a PVA meeting required before a Wayne County appeal?
faqs.a: Yes. The conference comes first, and the appeal is filed at the County Clerk's office by close of business on the day after the inspection period ends.

faqs.q: What does Wayne County's homestead exemption take off my assessment?
faqs.a: For 2025 and 2026 it takes $49,100 off the assessed value of your residence. Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply at the PVA.

faqs.q: Who gets my Wayne County tax bill after April 15?
faqs.a: The County Clerk. The bill becomes a certificate of delinquency with a lien, then picks up 1 percent monthly interest and commissions, and a third party may buy it 90 to 135 days later.
